s: A VPC spans three Availability Zones, each with public and private subnets. One NAT gateway and one internet gateway exist. Private EC2 instances must connect to the internet.
o: Add two more NAT gateways (one per AZ). Configure each private subnet to use its AZ's NAT gateway.
Add two more NAT gateways and configure public subnets.
Add internet gateways per AZ and route private subnets.
Add internet gateways per AZ and configure public subnets.
e: To improve resiliency and fault tolerance, place a NAT Gateway in each AZ, and route each private subnet to its local NAT gateway. This ensures local AZ failure won't break internet access. VPC NAT Gateway High Availability

w.y: Private instances in all three AZs share one NAT gateway, so an AZ failure cuts them off. The best-practice fix is one NAT gateway in each AZ's public subnet, with each private subnet routing to the NAT gateway in its own AZ.

o.A: Correct: one NAT gateway per AZ and AZ-local routes removes the single point of failure.
o.B: Routing has to change for the private subnets, not the public ones.
o.C: A VPC can have only one internet gateway, and private subnets do not route directly to it.
o.D: A VPC can have only one internet gateway, and it is already highly available.

st: Right for the exam; since Nov 2025 a Regional NAT gateway can also cover all AZs as one gateway, but questions written before then expect one NAT gateway per AZ.
